gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, at today's maker-store prices in the same $249–$349 range ChatGPT quoted for Bambu, a shopper can get a fully enclosed printer (Flashforge Adventurer 5M, $249 at flashforge.com) or a printer with four colours built in (Anycubic Kobra X 4-Color, $349 at store.anycubic.com), or that the 'best for batch' Elegoo Neptune 4 Max now costs $394 at Elegoo's store, not the ~$299–330 that 3dprintgearlab states.
standout_why: Compared against extruly (cited; it prices only Bambu: A1 mini + LED kit $249, A1 $305, P1S with no price), aemind (cited; Amazon prices from 2026-10-16: A1 $299.99, Kobra X $299.99, A1 mini kit $249), and the top result 3dprintgearlab (A1 mini $219–299, Ender 3 V3 SE ~$199, P1S+AMS $399–499 on sale, Neptune 4 Max ~$299–330). None of them gives today's maker-store prices. None lists an enclosed printer at the A1 mini's price, the built-in 4-colour Kobra X, or the QIDI and Flashforge models. 3dprintgearlab's Neptune 4 Max price is now $64–95 too low. Tom's Hardware (cited) would not load: both fetches returned only the title, so I could not check its picks.
decides: The A1 mini stays the default for PLA fidgets. extruly says its print quality is 'essentially identical' to the A1's, and it calls matte PLA the top filament, so enclosures and hot chambers add nothing for fidget toys. The pricing changes two branches of the answer. For colourful fidgets, the Kobra X 4-Color at $349 (Anycubic store) competes with the A1 mini Combo ($299.99 at Micro Center as ChatGPT showed, $369 on Amazon today). For a kids or family buyer at $249, the enclosed AD5M costs the same as the A1 mini LED kit. For batch selling, the Neptune 4 Max is no longer cheaper than the A1: $394 against $305.
